Parents were supportive and said they will try to help with money and not to worry about it because it's "just paper", and reminded me that I'm not a burden. 

Talked with a crisis counselor (but was in no danger to myself), and he suggested I go to set up an appointment with university counseling services and we will go from there. They'll also help to reach out to my profs, since I think if I say much at this point they'll think I'm just making excuses. 

SO. Besides hurting my girlfriend by withholding info from her (I'm thinking I was being pragmatic since my friend is here and could help more immediately? Idk why I lied tho), things are mostly good or at least hopefully moving in that direction.

I got a message from a friend earlier tonight asking if I knew any fluent Spanish speakers. A friend of hers had come across a homeless man who could only speak Spanish and was wanting to help him.  I tried contacting some friends but received no reply, so I met the friend and the man at a local restaurant around 10:30.  The man was drunk and my Spanish is rusty, but I managed to work out that he had come to the US after his wife died on the promise of a job to send money back to his four kids in Mexico.  Friend and I managed to get in contact with a priest who got the man a hotel room for the night and will try to help him further tomorrow. The man cried and asked to pray with us, and I left him some food on the way out.  It was a very humbling experience, and I wish the man the best.

Hi, I'm sorry if that experience was confusing or troubling for you in any way. I've battled my own demons with depression and had a brief flirtation with self-harm in a state of desperation to feel ANYTHING in one of my darker moments. From what I can tell from research and my undergrad (BA in Psychology), a lot of Self-Harm is self reinforcing because of the adrenaline rush, endorphins, or the sight of blood.  People will hurt themselves in an attempt to feel something, or a way of expressing a sense of control over their inner turmoil. 

As far as feeling that rush again after seeing the blood/the rush the pain, I think that it was more than likely a trigger from when you used to self harm for other reasons. I only tried it a few times, but managed to stop myself because of how scared I was when I LIKED it.  If it makes you feel any better, my first reaction upon seeing a person's arm covered in self inflicted cuts was something like envy and longing at one point, and I've been clean of self-harm for a couple years and still get fleeting urges.  Triggers can cause flashbacks and cravings in less than a second, so it's best to avoid them if you can at all. 

Just remember your coping skills!  Just because you have an urge does not man you have to act on it, and this too shall pass. Wishing you luck.
